To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

it is possible and useful to create scaled-down versions of Internet-like topologies that preserve the performance of the original system, and that the resulting performance can be extrapolated to the expected performance on the original topology.

(1) it is possible to downscale the Internet by removing the links that are not congested and that the performance of this scaled topology is very similar to the original topology, and (2) it is possible, using a scaled topology, to simulate the performance of the Internet up to two orders faster than simulating its full topology.

it is possible (i) to downscale the topology of the network while preserving its performance and (ii) to do so with a speedup of up to two orders in magnitude, thus enabling the use of simulations to study large networks.

preserving the performance of Internet-like networks by scaling down their topologies.
